editorial_checks: The Hanan judgment concerns Germany's procedural investigative obligation, not the substantive legality or complete attribution of the airstrike.
The jurisdictional link rests on special features in combination; merely opening a domestic inquiry is not presented as universally sufficient.
The independence complaint concerning the investigation in Germany was manifestly ill-founded; exhaustion was left open, not used as the ground of rejection.
Initial defects, later examination, the possibility of reopening and limits on file access remain visible; an adverse result is not described as no hearing ever occurring.
Parliamentary disagreement, criminal-law findings, Convention review and reparation are distinguished. No contested total casualty figure is adopted.
UK departure, Great Britain/UK geography, the original Protocol and the later Windsor adjustments are distinguished.
Domestic effect is attributed to Parliament's statutory mechanism, not to foreign rules overriding Parliament by their own force.

The Stormont Brake concerns specified amended/replacement acts and requires more than thirty signatures. New acts/applicability motions and the separate Article 18 continuation vote are not conflated.
The 2024 vote continued Articles 5–10 by a simple majority without cross-community support; this triggered review, not automatic expiry or a membership/unification referendum.
The Northern Ireland history stops at end-2025. Publication of a government response is not evidence of completed implementation or a current customs guide.
No invented driver, witness, private thought, dialogue or composite victim. The two histories are not treated as equivalent harms or proof of a non-coercive theoretical model.
